1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account solely from the server-side session cookie via authenticatedSession(), which checks session.userId === account.id and the required stage; no client-supplied identifier is ever trusted.

2.why: The identity verification code is hashed and stored on the individual session record (session.identityCodeHash) and matched only against that session, so a code cannot be replayed by another session/user.

3.why: The /api/mfa/activate handler sets account.mfaEnabled and new backup codes but never iterates the sessions map to revoke other sessions, so any previously created session entries remain valid until idle/absolute timeout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (encryptSecret) and backup codes are stored as salted, peppered SHA-256 digests with only a 'used' flag, never plaintext.

5.why: Identity codes, backup codes, salts, session IDs and CSRF tokens all use node:crypto randomBytes, but the OTP shared secret is a hardcoded constant (EVALUATION_TOTP_SECRET = "JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP") rather than CSPRNG-generated.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the session cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, though the provisioning secret, test OTP and backup codes are held in JS variables and printed into an in-page log panel.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validRecovery, base32 regex) strictly constrain all inputs, JSON bodies are type-checked, and there is no SQL/data store to inject into.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent (log, message, dds[i].textContent); the only innerHTML use is a static, data-free <dt>/<dd> skeleton, and CSP uses nonces with no unsafe-inline.

9.why: The only redirect-like parameter is validated against a single literal allow-listed value (input.redirect !== "/verify-identity" is rejected) and no Location redirect is ever issued from user input.

10.why: securityHeaders() sets nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on HTML, API and error responses.

11.why: sessionCookie()/clearCookie() emit 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' with Max-Age matching the absolute session lifetime.

12.why: Stack traces are suppressed (generic 500/400 messages), but the /api/signin response returns testCode and the client console.logs and DOM-renders the identity code, the provisioning secret and the full list of backup codes.

13.why: The identity code has identityCodeUsed plus a 5-minute expiry, TOTP counters are recorded in lastAcceptedTotpCounter to block reuse within the window, and backup codes are flagged used on acceptance.

14.why: failure() increments per-session and per-account counters and imposes a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures on identity, activate, check and recovery endpoints, though /api/signin itself is not rate-limited.

15.why: Successful identity verification deletes the old session and issues a brand-new ID via newSession("authenticated"), authenticatedSession() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
